1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. EMR: Elastic MapReduce; ORC: Optimized Row Columnar; JDBC: Java Database Connectivity; RDS: Relational Database Service; SSL: Secure Sockets Layer; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; NAT: network address translation; AI: artificial intelligence; EBS: Elastic Block Store

  • Explain what a data catalog is and why query engines need one
  • Build and reference a technical catalog: the AWS Glue Data Catalog and an Apache Hive metastore
  • Discover schemas and populate the catalog with AWS Glue crawlers
  • Synchronize partitions with the catalog
  • Create connections for cataloging
  • Create and manage a business data catalog in Amazon SageMaker Catalog

2What a Catalog Is and Why It Matters (skills 2.2.1 and 2.2.2)

Running case

Kestrel Freight Finds Its Data

  • New order files appear in S3 every day in new folders
  • Analysts cannot tell which table is the real one or what a column means
  • Athena, Glue and EMR must all see the same tables
  • Your job: build one technical catalog for the engines and one business catalog for the people

  • A data catalog is a central store of metadata (data about data): where the data is, its format and schema, its partitions, and often what it means and who owns it
  • Technical catalog: for engines and engineers: databases, tables, columns and types, partitions, locations, formats
  • Business catalog: for people: business terms, descriptions, owners, data products, and access requests
  • Schema-on-read: the data stays in S3 as files; the catalog tells engines how to read them
AWS Glue Data Catalog Apache Hive metastore
What Managed, serverless central metadata repository, Hive metastore compatible The open-source metadata service of the Hadoop world
Used by Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, Glue, Lake Formation, SageMaker Spark, Hive, Presto on self-managed or EMR clusters
Choose it when You want one managed catalog for all AWS analytics You already run a Hive metastore (you can point EMR at the Glue Data Catalog instead to remove the metastore to manage)
  • Glue Data Catalog parts: databases (containers of tables), tables (schema, location, format, partition keys), partitions, connections, crawlers, classifiers and schema registries for streaming schemas
  • Use a catalog to consume data from its source: query by table name in Athena (SELECT ... FROM sales.orders) and in Glue jobs (from_catalog), instead of hard-coding S3 paths and schemas
  • Lake Formation adds permissions on catalog databases and tables (Module 15)
Exam tip

"Athena, EMR and Glue must share table definitions" → the AWS Glue Data Catalog (set it as the Hive metastore for EMR).

3Glue Crawlers: Discovering Schemas (skill 2.2.3)

  • A crawler scans a data store, infers the format and schema, and creates or updates tables and partitions in the Data Catalog
  • Steps: run custom classifiers in order (the first match wins), else built-in classifiers (JSON, CSV, Avro, Parquet, ORC and more); connect to the store; infer the schema; write metadata; each table gets a classification label
  • Data stores: S3, JDBC databases (RDS, Aurora, Redshift and others), DynamoDB, MongoDB and DocumentDB, Delta, Iceberg and Hudi tables, and more
  • Schedule a crawler (on demand, cron, or on an event) so new files, columns and partitions are found; a Glue trigger starts at most two crawlers
  • Partitions: when most folders at a level have similar schemas, the crawler makes partitions (year=2026/month=11/) of one table; to make separate tables, give each table root its own include path
  • Update behavior: choose what happens when the schema changes (update the table definition or ignore) and when objects disappear (delete from the catalog, mark as deprecated, or ignore)
  • Athena tip: in Athena one table = one S3 prefix; objects with different schemas under one prefix can give empty results: separate include paths
Exam tip

"New daily folders appear and the table must pick up the new partitions and columns automatically" → a scheduled (or event-driven) Glue crawler.

4Synchronizing Partitions (skill 2.2.4)

  • Partitions split a table by key values so queries read only the needed folders; the catalog must know each partition before engines can use it
  • Hive-style layout: s3://bucket/sales/year=2026/month=11/day=07/ (key=value in the path)
Way to sync Use when
Glue crawler (scheduled or event-driven) Easy, automatic; also detects schema changes
Athena MSCK REPAIR TABLE Hive-style paths (lowercase key names, s3:// locations) are in S3 but missing from the table
Athena ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION Non-Hive layout (for example 2026/11/07/) or a single known partition; use IF NOT EXISTS
Glue API BatchCreatePartition or a job writing with partition updates Pipelines that create partitions as they write
Partition projection (Athena) Highly partitioned, predictable layouts: Athena computes partitions from table properties instead of looking them up, so no sync is needed and queries are faster
Partition indexes (Glue) Tables with very many partitions: faster partition lookup (Athena cannot read more than 1 million partitions in one scan)
  • Keep each table in its own folder hierarchy, or MSCK REPAIR TABLE can attach partitions of one table to another
Exam tip

"Hundreds of thousands of date partitions make Athena planning slow" → partition projection or partition indexes. "Firehose writes 2026/11/07/ folders" (non-Hive) → ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION or partition projection.

5Connections for Cataloging (skill 2.2.5)

  • A Glue connection stores how to reach a data store: type (JDBC, MongoDB, Kafka, Salesforce and more), host and port, credentials (use AWS Secrets Manager), SSL settings, and the VPC, subnet and security groups if the store is private
  • Use a connection in a crawler (to catalog a JDBC table), in a job (read and write) or for Kafka sources
  • Network rules: security groups must allow the Glue connection to reach the store; for stores outside AWS use a NAT gateway path; a job can use JDBC connections in one subnet
  • New source or target connection: create the connection, test it, attach it to a crawler or job, and crawl to catalog the tables
  • Keep credentials out of the console fields: reference a secret
Exam tip

"A crawler cannot reach a private RDS database" → check the connection's VPC, subnet and security group, and that the secret is valid.

6Business Data Catalogs: Amazon SageMaker Catalog (skill 2.2.6)Verify live

  • Amazon SageMaker Catalog is the business data catalog of Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio: it helps people discover, understand, govern and share data and AI assets
  • It builds on the technical metadata (for example tables in the Glue Data Catalog) and adds a business layer:
    • Assets: the datasets and resources that are published to the catalog
    • Business glossary: shared business terms with one meaning (for example "delivered order")
    • Metadata forms: custom fields (owner, sensitivity, refresh rate) attached to assets
    • Data products: groups of related assets packaged for consumers
    • Publish and subscribe: producers publish; consumers search and request a subscription; the owner approves, and access is granted
  • It works inside domains, domain units and projects (Module 14), which organize teams and control who can see and use what
  • Lineage (Module 9) and access (Module 18) are managed through the same catalog
Glue Data Catalog SageMaker Catalog
Audience Engines and engineers Analysts, data owners and stewards
Content Schemas, partitions, locations Glossary, descriptions, owners, data products, subscriptions
Question it answers "How do I read this?" "What is this, who owns it, may I use it?"
Exam tip

"Analysts need to search, understand and request access to datasets with business terms" → Amazon SageMaker Catalog (a business catalog). "The engine needs schemas and partitions" → Glue Data Catalog (a technical catalog).

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1New dated folders (year=2026/month=11/day=08) arrive in S3 daily with occasional new columns. The table in the Data Catalog must update automatically. Which solution fits best?

  • AManually edit the table each day
  • BA larger Athena workgroup
  • CA scheduled AWS Glue crawler
  • DS3 Transfer Acceleration
Show the answer

Answer: C. A scheduled crawler discovers new partitions and schema changes and updates the table.

S2Data is stored under Hive-style paths such as year=2026/month=11/ and a new partition is missing from an Athena table. Which TWO actions add it? (Select TWO.)

  • AConvert the files to CSV
  • BRun a Glue crawler on the table's location
  • CIncrease the Athena query timeout
  • DDelete the table's S3 prefix
  • ERun MSCK REPAIR TABLE
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. MSCK REPAIR TABLE loads Hive-style partitions into the table, and a crawler also discovers them. The other actions do not register partitions.

S3An Athena table has several hundred thousand date partitions and query planning is slow. The partition layout is predictable. What is the best improvement?

  • AMove the data to Amazon EBS
  • BPartition projection
  • CDisable partitioning
  • DUse gzip-compressed CSV
Show the answer

Answer: B. Partition projection computes partition values and locations from table properties instead of reading them from the catalog, which speeds up planning for predictable layouts.

S4A crawler must catalog tables in a private Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database. Which item is REQUIRED for the crawler to connect?

  • AA Glue connection with the VPC, subnet, security groups and a secret for credentials
  • BAn S3 bucket policy that allows the crawler's role to list the bucket and read the objects
  • CA Kinesis data stream that carries the database change records
  • DAn EventBridge schedule rule that starts the crawler every night
Show the answer

Answer: A. A Glue connection holds how to reach the data store, including network settings and credentials, which the crawler uses to connect.

S5Business analysts want to search for datasets using business terms, see who owns them and request access, with owner approval. Which service feature fits best?

  • AAmazon SageMaker Catalog with a business glossary and subscriptions
  • BThe AWS Glue Data Catalog alone, with table and column names and partition values
  • CAmazon S3 Inventory reports delivered to a central bucket
  • DAWS CloudTrail event history for the analysts' accounts
Show the answer

Answer: A. SageMaker Catalog is a business catalog with glossary terms, data products and a publish and subscribe workflow with approval, built on top of technical metadata.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Catalog Metadata about data: location, schema, partitions, meaning; technical (engines) vs business (people)
Glue Data Catalog Managed, Hive-compatible; databases, tables, partitions, connections; shared by Athena, EMR, Spectrum, Glue, Lake Formation
Hive metastore Open-source; EMR can use the Glue Data Catalog instead
Crawler Classifiers (custom first, then built-in) → infer schema → tables and partitions; scheduled; separate include paths for separate tables; update and delete behavior
Partitions Hive-style key=value; sync by crawler, MSCK REPAIR TABLE, ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION, API; partition projection and partition indexes for many partitions
Connections Type, host, secret (Secrets Manager), SSL, VPC/subnet/security groups; used by crawlers and jobs
SageMaker Catalog Business catalog: assets, glossary, metadata forms, data products, publish/subscribe with approval; in SageMaker Unified Studio domains and projects
